papers.title_en: ABot-AgentOS: A General Robotic Agent OS with Lifelong Multi-modal Memory
papers.authors: Jiayi Tian, Shiao Liu, Yuting Xu, Jia Lu, Zihao Guan, Honglin Han, Di Yang, Minqi Gu, Yifei Qian, Tianlin Zhang, Yanqing Zhu, Zeqian Ye, Menglin Yang, Fei Wang, Xu Hu, Xiuxian Li, Wei Zhang, Shihui Su, Yiyan Ji, Jingbo Wang, Ziteng Feng, Jiaheng Liu, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Xiaolong Wu, Zixiao Tang, Zhining Gu, Yang Cai, Linbo Zheng, Jingjing Ma, Mingyang Yin, Zedong Chu, Ziqiao Li, Mu Xu
papers.evidence: 提供通用机器人操作系统，支持导航等众多任务
papers.tldr: 现有VLM/VLA系统在长时程具身任务中缺乏通用运行时层，导致推理、记忆和跨本体执行受限。本文提出ABot-AgentOS，一个通用机器人Agent操作系统，包含场景条件规划、上下文隔离技能执行、多模态图记忆和故障驱动自进化循环。在EmbodiedWorldBench基准上，ABot-AgentOS显著提升任务成功率；在LoCoMo、OpenEQA等记忆基准上取得最高89.0的分数。这一工作为机器人提供了可持久化和审计的通用Agent层，促进持续交互与自我改进。
papers.abstract_en: Recent VLM and VLA systems have improved robotic perception and action prediction, yet long-horizon embodied agents still require a general runtime layer for reasoning, memory, tool use, verification, and cross-embodiment execution. We present ABot-AgentOS, a general robotic Agent Operating System that sits above low-level controllers and provides a deliberative agent layer for scene-conditioned planning, context-isolated skill execution, multi-stage verification, multi-modal memory, and edge-cloud collaboration. To evaluate such systems, we introduce EmbodiedWorldBench, an executable benchmark with 16 indoor, outdoor, and hybrid scenes, four difficulty levels, and over 200 tasks involving navigation, object search, NPC dialogue, dynamic events, and trace-grounded scoring. ABot-AgentOS further introduces Universal Multi-modal Graph Memory, a persistent source-grounded substrate that converts dialogue, visual observations, spatial context, temporal relations, and task traces into typed nodes and edges. A failure-driven self-evolution loop converts diagnosed memory failures into gated runtime evo-assets that are promoted only to later evaluation splits, preventing current-split ground-truth leakage while enabling continual improvement. On an initial EmbodiedWorldBench subset, ABot-AgentOS improves over a single-controller baseline in both task success and goal completion. Across memory benchmarks, ABot-AgentOS Static achieves 87.5 on LoCoMo, 59.9 on OpenEQA EM-EQA, 88.6 on Mem-Gallery, and 76.5 Acc@All on NExT-QA; self-evolution further improves LoCoMo to 88.7, OpenEQA to 60.4, and Mem-Gallery to 89.0. These results suggest that a general Agent OS layer can improve long-horizon embodied execution while providing persistent, auditable memory for continual interaction.

papers.title_en: Dual-Process Atomic Skill Learning: Decoupling Semantic Reasoning and Real-Time Control
papers.authors: Jun Chen, Erdent Bao, Wenlong Dong, Jierui Liu, Qi Cai, Hao Wan, Shaopeng Li, Weijun Qin, Jing Liang, Huiping Zhuang
papers.evidence: 语言条件模仿学习用于指令跟随
papers.tldr: 语言条件模仿学习在多步组合任务上泛化困难，现有层次方法因技能推理与动作生成紧密耦合导致训练不稳定和码本崩溃。受双过程理论启发，提出异步解耦框架DASL，用慢频率策略（向量量化）预测离散技能，高频率策略（潜扩散+决策Transformer）生成动作。实验表明，DASL显著优于基线，提升了技能获取和组合泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Language-conditioned Imitation Learning (IL) is essential for enabling robots to perform complex tasks following natural language instructions. However, generalizing to multi-step compositional tasks remains a significant challenge. While hierarchical approaches attempt to address this by decomposing tasks into atomic skills, existing methods often suffer from training instability and codebook collapse due to the tight coupling between high-level skill reasoning and low-level action generation in joint training paradigms. Inspired by the Dual-Process Theory of cognition, we propose Dual-Process Atomic Skill Learning (DASL), a novel asynchronous hierarchical imitation learning framework that decouples slow semantic reasoning from fast, real-time motion control. DASL comprises a Slow-Frequency Policy that predicts interpretable, discrete skills via Vector Quantization, and a High-Frequency Policy that leverages a latent diffusion model and a Decision Transformer to generate precise actions conditioned on these latent skills. By asynchronously coordinating these modules and utilizing diffusion to structure the latent space, our framework mitigates the skill codebook interference problem common in joint training paradigms. Evaluations across simulation benchmarks and experiment demonstrate that DASL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, excelling in skill acquisition and compositional generalization to unseen instructions. GitHub page: https://github.com/Hatakekaka/DASL

papers.title_en: CoRe: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Image Comparative Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.authors: Lin Peng, Cong Wan, Zeyu Guo, SongLin Dong, Yihong Gong
papers.evidence: 跨图像比较推理，涵盖空间关系、深度和距离
papers.tldr: 跨图像比较推理需要细粒度属性定位和全局一致性推理，现有VLM表现不佳。CoRe框架包含自动构建的CoRe-20K数据集、基于GRPO的TriSR结构化奖励机制和专属CoRe-Bench基准。在CoRe-Bench上比最强基线提升28.2分，同时保持标准基准竞争力。该工作为跨图像推理提供了统一框架和有价值的基准。
papers.abstract_en: Cross-image comparative reasoning remains challenging for vision-language models (VLMs), especially when correct prediction requires fine-grained attribute grounding and globally consistent reasoning. We present CoRe, a unified framework for this problem. CoRe includes: (i) CoRe-20K, a large-scale triplet-based training set automatically constructed from structured visual metadata through a multi-expert collaborative pipeline, covering counting, depth, distance, and spatial relations; (ii) TriSR, a structured reward framework that jointly supervises attribute grounding, judgment alignment, and triplet consistency under GRPO optimization; and (iii) CoRe-Bench, the first benchmark dedicated to fine-grained cross-image comparative reasoning. Experiments show that CoRe substantially outperforms existing VLMs on CoRe-Bench while remaining competitive on standard multimodal benchmarks, achieving a 28.2-point gain in partial accuracy over the strongest baseline.
